title: Bond role was ‘Josh O’Connor’s to lose’ but actor pulled out of the running, report suggests
text:
Josh O’Connor, one of the actors on the final shortlist for the role of James Bond which was ultimately won by Robert Pattinson, was an early favourite of director Denis Villeneuve but pulled out of the contest before a decision was made, it has been reported.
Writing in Puck’s What I’m Hearing newsletter, Matthew Belloni (who correctly forecast that Pattinson would win the role) said that O’Connor “had reservations about the baggage associated with the role from the start” and pulled out shortly after his test.
O’Connor, who previously played Prince Charles in The Crown and had a string of acclaimed independent movies under his belt, including God’s Own Country, La Chimera and The Mastermind, was reported to be in the initial three strong final shortlist for Bond, along with Callum Turner and Jack Lowden. The subsequent revelation that producers had also added Pattinson and How to Rob a Bank star Nicholas Hoult to the shortlist suggested that none of the original three were going to be cast.
According to Belloni, O’Connor “was actually an early favourite of director Denis Villeneuve, so much so that several insiders believed the gig was his to lose”, but his doubts meant that “he backed in and out of testing before deciding to do it – and soon afterward took himself out of the running”.
Belloni also suggested that another small detail in the pre-test deal that studio Amazon MGM struck with Pattinson indicated their eagerness to cast him; Pattinson was not obliged to commit to synchronise his personal branding partnerships with that of the Bond films. Brand partnerships have historically been a huge source of revenue for the Bond franchise and, on the face of it, Pattinson’s already-existing endorsements with watches and clothing brands could well cause a clash further down the line. Belloni says the issue “will now be negotiated”.
